solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Snatcher with crew put time into con

parts.note: a rowing eight is a boat's crew

indicators.note: put into tells us one piece goes inside the word for con

parts.note: a convict serving a life sentence is a lifer

explanation.surface: A swindle: someone recruits a gang and slips time into a con trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snatcher' looks like a thief, but the snatch is a weightlifting lift.
explanation.definitionFit: The snatch is one of the two Olympic lifts, so an athlete performing it is a snatcher.

clue.text: See weight condition when topless

indicators.note: topless means the word for condition loses its first letter

parts.note: physical condition is fitness

explanation.surface: Checking your weight and physical condition without a shirt on.
explanation.definitionFit: To witness something is to see it happen with your own eyes.

clue.text: Ready after hip implant

indicators.note: after places the word for ready after the word for hip

parts.note: hip means fashionable, in
ready, as in all set

explanation.surface: Someone is ready to go after a hip replacement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hip' and 'implant' point to surgery, but hip means trendy.
explanation.definitionFit: An inset is a piece put into something larger, which is an implant.

clue.text: Consider characteristic of Dali's Agony of Love

parts.note: to hear a case is to consider it
Salvador Dali was famous for his upturned moustache, a tache

explanation.surface: Thinking about a feature of a supposed Dali painting titled Agony of Love.
explanation.walkthrough: TACHE is British slang for a moustache.
explanation.definitionFit: The agony of love is emotional anguish over a lost love.

clue.text: Left hand spread on a surface

parts.note: to give a hand is to give aid

explanation.surface: A left hand spread flat on a table.
explanation.definitionFit: Laid out flat on a table, as a cloth or carpet is put down, is spread on a surface.

clue.text: Slight criticism when each son gives way to female deception

indicators.note: each son giving way means every letter for son is replaced by the letter for female

parts.note: slight means slim, thin

indicators.note: each says the same swap of the son's letter for the female's letter happens in the second word too

parts.note: a slam is a harsh criticism

explanation.surface: Mild criticism when every son yields to a woman is a sham.
explanation.walkthrough: 'each' says both S letters change, giving FLIM and FLAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Flimflam is nonsense or a swindle, so it is deception.

clue.text: Hail upset daughter on eastern bypass

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the word for hail is turned upside down

parts.note: ave is the Latin greeting hail

explanation.surface: A hail storm forces a daughter onto an eastern bypass road.
explanation.definitionFit: To evade something is to get round it, to bypass it.

clue.text: Double vision could result from rum used with such forgetfulness

indicators.note: rum, meaning odd, signals the letters of double vision are rearranged together with another word

explanation.surface: Drinking rum can bring on double vision and drunken forgetting.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer plus USED makes an anagram of DOUBLE VISION; 'rum' reads as the drink but is the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Oblivion is the state of having forgotten everything, total forgetfulness.

clue.text: Going north, say, in European city to find another

indicators.note: in puts the reversed piece inside the capital's name

parts.note: Bern is the Swiss capital

indicators.note: in a down clue going north means reading upwards, reversed

parts.note: eg means for example, say

explanation.surface: Travelling north from a European city to find a second one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going north' turns EG into GE; 'another' refers back to the European city.
explanation.definitionFit: Bergen is a city in Norway, so another European city.

clue.text: Maestro knocked back lush cold sandwiches, abandoning piano

indicators.note: knocked back, like a drink, signals the word for lush is read in reverse

parts.note: a lush is a drunkard, a sot
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

indicators.note: abandoning signals that the letter for piano is dropped from the sandwiches

parts.note: panini are Italian toasted sandwiches
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A drunk downs cold sandwiches and walks away from the piano recital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' turns SOT into TOS; 'abandoning' removes P from PANINI, leaving ANINI.
explanation.definitionFit: Arturo Toscanini was a celebrated Italian conductor, and maestro is the honorific for a great conductor.

clue.text: Toddler does this better after outsiders leave

indicators.note: outsiders leaving means the first and last letters of the word for better are removed

parts.note: a better is one who bets, a gambler

explanation.surface: A small child improves once the strangers have gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' reads as an adjective but is the noun: one who bets.
explanation.definitionFit: A toddler walks slowly and unsteadily, so an easy stroll describes its gait as a verb.

clue.text: Being married in ill-will must become ultimately repellent

indicators.note: must become tells us one letter is swapped for another in the word for ill-will

parts.note: ill-will is enmity, hostility

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of repellent

explanation.surface: Being married amid hostility is bound to turn repellent in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: An entity is anything that exists in its own right, a being.

clue.text: Around fine iron, seal gift

parts.note: O is a round shape, so around can give O
F is the pencil abbreviation for fine
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
a signet ring is used to seal documents

explanation.surface: A present is assembled from fine iron and a seal.
explanation.definitionFit: An offering is something given, especially as a present or tribute.

clue.text: Helping to squeeze uniform that's really wet

indicators.note: to squeeze says the word for helping grips another letter inside

parts.note: a helping of cake is a slice
U is uniform in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A serving of food is pressed into a uniform that is soaking.
explanation.definitionFit: To sluice is to drench or flush with a rush of water, wetting thoroughly.

clue.text: Idealists cast out instruments with no love

indicators.note: cast, as in thrown, means the letters of out are rearranged
with no means the letter for love is dropped

parts.note: pianos are musical instruments
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Idealists throw out musical instruments, having no love for them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' turns OUT into UTO; dropping O from PIANOS leaves PIANS.
explanation.definitionFit: Utopians dream of an ideal society, so they are idealists.

clue.text: Interjection of joy interrupting old master from island

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into the painter's name

parts.note: Titian was a Venetian Renaissance painter, an Old Master
ah is a cry of delight

explanation.surface: A cry of joy breaks in on an Old Master who hails from an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Tahiti is a South Pacific island, so a native or thing from there is Tahitian.

clue.text: Fresh sandwiches lead to red rash

indicators.note: sandwiches means the word for fresh holds a letter inside

parts.note: fresh, as in cheeky, impudent

indicators.note: lead to points to the first letter of red

explanation.surface: Fresh sandwiches cause a red skin rash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rash' looks like a skin complaint but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Imprudent means acting without care for consequences, which is rash.

clue.text: Dinosaurs go off with adult, after shaking T Rex died

indicators.note: off, as in gone wrong, signals the letters are rearranged, after shaking off T

parts.note: R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Dinosaurs rot away with an adult, after shaking off a T. Rex that died.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' (gone bad) is the anagram signal, and 'after shaking T' strips that letter from the pool; 'Dinosaurs' means reactionaries, not reptiles.
explanation.definitionFit: Dinosaurs is a jokey word for old-fashioned people, the old guard resisting change.

clue.text: Disorganised start to school fair opened by knight

indicators.note: start to points to the first letter of school
opened by means the word for fair is split with a letter put inside

parts.note: fair as in beautiful, lovely
N is knight in chess notation

explanation.surface: A school fair gets off to a shambolic start once a knight opens it.
explanation.definitionFit: Slovenly means untidy and careless in habits, which is being disorganised.

clue.text: Part of code for opening plant

definitions.meaning: open ... is the password that opens the cave in Ali Baba
a herb grown for its seeds

explanation.surface: A fragment of a password for opening a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Its seeds are used in cooking, and it is the magic word from Ali Baba.

clue.text: Disclose revolutionary French article after work pressure

indicators.note: after places the French piece after the work

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work

indicators.note: revolutionary means the French word is turned round

parts.note: une is the French feminine indefinite article
P is the symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Revealing a revolutionary French article written after work under pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: To open up is to talk freely, revealing what was kept back.

clue.text: Acclaim place to be above scrutiny

indicators.note: in a down clue, being above places the abbreviation first

parts.note: an audit is an official scrutiny of accounts

explanation.surface: Acclaim gives a place where you are beyond scrutiny.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaudit is an expression of praise or approval, acclaim.

clue.text: I slap leg wound, causing upset

indicators.note: wound, as in twisted, shows the letters are wound into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone slaps a leg wound and makes a fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wound' reads as an injury but is the past tense of wind.
explanation.definitionFit: An upset of a cup is a spillage, the noun for something knocked over.

clue.text: Philosopher to engage in conversation

indicators.note: in conversation means the word is spoken, giving a homophone

parts.note: gears engage when they lock together

explanation.surface: A philosopher who likes to engage in conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: John Locke was an English philosopher.
explanation.definitionFit: John Locke was a leading English Enlightenment philosopher.

clue.text: Swimmer's opening letters of abuse thrown in water

indicators.note: opening means the first letter of swimmer's
thrown means the letters of abuse are flung into disorder

explanation.surface: A swimmer begins hurling abuse into the water.
explanation.definitionFit: Subsea describes what lies or happens beneath the surface of the sea.

clue.text: Gangster nearly covers back

indicators.note: covers means the words contain the answer within them

explanation.surface: A gangster nearly provides cover for someone's back.
explanation.definitionFit: The stern is the rear part of a ship, its back.

clue.text: Drive second leg

parts.note: pins is slang for legs

explanation.definitionFit: A spin is a short pleasure drive in a car.

clue.text: Busy boss, possibly?

definitions.meaning: a boss is a man in charge, abbreviated man i/c

explanation.surface: A frantic boss, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: I/C is short for in charge, so a boss is a MAN I/C.
explanation.definitionFit: Manic means frenziedly active, which is busy taken to an extreme.

clue.text: Note height borne by tag on collar

indicators.note: borne by means carried inside the word for tag on

parts.note: to tag on is to append
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A musical note and height measurement attached to a tag on a dog collar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collar' looks like a noun for a dog but is the police verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To collar a suspect is slang for arresting them, which is to apprehend.

clue.text: Try avoiding a number gripped by clear primal urge

indicators.note: avoiding means the a is left out of the word for try

parts.note: to try a case in court is to hear it

indicators.note: gripped by means held inside the word for clear

parts.note: clear as in distinct, plain

explanation.surface: An attempt to dodge a number held by a basic primal urge.
explanation.definitionFit: The impulse to follow the crowd is a primitive social drive, a basic urge.
